steps.domain_action: Initialize the system with the target integer N in an uninitialized state.
Establish the critical threshold where scale-free correlations emerge for the search.
Begin the forward morphism by calculating the initial candidate square a² = ceil(sqrt(N))².
Fork the evaluation into two branches: one to test if (a² - N) is a perfect square, one to test if it is not.
In the T-arm, affirmatively check if the remainder r = a² - N is a perfect square b².
Compose the arithmetic operations to compute b = sqrt(r) if the T-arm condition holds.
In the F-arm, negatively refute the current candidate if r is not a perfect square.
In the F-arm, descend to the next candidate by incrementing a and recalculating the difference.
Hold the symmetric decomposition paradox where N is both composite and decomposed during the transition.
Rejoin the T and F arms to resolve whether the current candidate yields a valid factorization.
Chain the successful factor extraction (a-b) and (a+b) if the T-arm was affirmed.
Permanently record the found factor pair and the integer winding invariant.
Anchor the system at the boundary condition where the search space collapses to the solution.
Re-enter the self-referential state to confirm the factorization identity holds.
